subject: FRE
label: Grade 01
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 01 French, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Greetings and introductions
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Greetings and introductions', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: introduce myself in French. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Greetings and introductions' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: introduce myself in French, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: Bonjour, je m'appelle [mon prenom]. Et toi? Je m'appelle [mon prenom]. Enchante. Comment ca va? Ca va bien, merci. Method: Model run for 'Greetings and introductions'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Introduce myself in French: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Say hello and your name. Bonjour ! [Hello!] Je m'appelle [mon prénom]. [My name is (your name).] Say your own first name in place of [mon prénom]. Use Salut ! [Hi!] with friends and Bonjour with teachers. Practise standing up and saying it clearly.

Step 2, Ask and answer about age and feelings. Tu as quel âge ? [How old are you?] J'ai six ans. [I am six years old.] Ça va ? [How are you?] Ça va bien, merci. [I am fine, thank you.] Note J'ai, not Je suis, for age.

Step 3, Act out a first meeting. Élève A : Bonjour ! Comment tu t'appelles ? [Hello! What is your name?] Élève B : Je m'appelle [mon prénom]. Et toi ? [My name is (my name). And you?] Élève A : Enchantée ! [Nice to meet you!] Élève B : Enchanté ! [Nice to meet you!]

Step 4, Say goodbye politely. Au revoir ! [Goodbye!] À demain ! [See you tomorrow!] Merci, madame. [Thank you, madam.] S'il vous plaît. [Please.] Say each phrase with the right gesture: wave for au revoir and nod for merci.

Step 5, Fix a common error. A child says Je suis appelle [mon prénom]. Correction: Je m'appelle [mon prénom], never je suis appelle. Another slip is Je suis six ans; say J'ai six ans, because French says I have six years.

Step 6, Your turn: introduce yourself with name, age and a goodbye. Model answer: Bonjour ! Je m'appelle [mon prénom]. J'ai sept ans. Ça va bien, merci. Au revoir ! [Hello! My name is (my name). I am seven. I am fine, thank you. Goodbye!]

modules.title: Numbers and colours
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Numbers and colours', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: say numbers and colours. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Numbers and colours' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: say numbers and colours, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq. rouge, bleu, vert. 'J'ai trois stylos bleus.' Method: Model run for 'Numbers and colours'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Say numbers and colours: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Count from one to ten: un, deux, trois, quatre, cinq, six, sept, huit, neuf, dix. Say them with your fingers. The final x of deux is silent, but the x of dix sounds like s, and the t of huit is pronounced. Repeat three times, getting faster.

Step 2, Learn colours: rouge [red], bleu [blue], jaune [yellow], vert [green], noir [black], blanc [white]. Hold up coloured objects and ask: C'est de quelle couleur ? [What colour is it?] Answer: C'est rouge. [It is red.]

Step 3, Put numbers and things together. J'ai trois crayons. [I have three pencils.] J'ai deux balles rouges. [I have two red balls.] Combien de pommes ? [How many apples?] Cinq pommes. [Five apples.] Practise with real objects on your desk.

Step 4, Dialogue with a friend. Élève A : Quelle est ta couleur préférée ? [What is your favourite colour?] Élève B : Ma couleur préférée est le bleu. [My favourite colour is blue.] Élève A : Moi, j'aime le vert. [I like green.] Élève B : Super ! [Great!]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says un balle. Correction: une balle, because balle is feminine. Say un crayon but une gomme. With colours, many add an e for feminine: une pomme verte [a green apple], une chaise blanche [a white chair].

Step 6, Your turn: say you have four yellow pencils and one blue ball. Model answer: J'ai quatre crayons jaunes et une balle bleue. [I have four yellow pencils and a blue ball.] Then ask a friend: Combien de crayons ? [How many pencils?]

modules.title: Fruits and food
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Fruits and food', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: name fruits and food. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Fruits and food' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: name fruits and food, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: une pomme (apple), une banane, du pain (bread), de l'eau (water). 'Je voudrais une pomme, s'il vous plait.' Method: Model run for 'Fruits and food'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Name fruits and food: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Learn fruit names with articles. la pomme [the apple], la banane [the banana], la fraise [the strawberry], l'orange [the orange], le raisin [the grapes]. Note that l' is used before a vowel. Say them while looking at pictures.

Step 2, Learn food words: le pain [bread], le lait [milk], le fromage [cheese], l'eau [water], le gâteau [cake]. Ask: Qu'est-ce que c'est ? [What is it?] Answer: C'est du pain. [It is some bread.] Practise with picture cards.

Step 3, Say what you like. J'aime les bananes. [I like bananas.] J'aime les fraises. [I like strawberries.] Je n'aime pas le fromage. [I do not like cheese.] Use les for plural fruit you like in general.

Step 4, Order at the table. Maman : Tu as faim ? [Are you hungry?] L'enfant : Oui, j'ai faim ! [Yes, I am hungry!] Maman : Tu veux une pomme ? [Do you want an apple?] L'enfant : Oui, merci. Je voudrais aussi de l'eau, s'il te plaît. [Yes, thank you. I would also like some water, please.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A child says J'aime le bananes. Correction: J'aime les bananes, because the noun is plural and needs les. Another error is une lait; say du lait or le lait, because lait is masculine.

Step 6, Your turn: say you like strawberries and do not like cheese, then ask for bread politely. Model answer: J'aime les fraises. Je n'aime pas le fromage. Je voudrais du pain, s'il vous plaît. [I like strawberries. I do not like cheese. I would like some bread, please.]

modules.title: Days of the week and months
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Days of the week and months', taught in a way that is short, playful, with objects, pictures and talk. The target is clear: say the days and months. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Days of the week and months' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: say the days and months, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. 'Aujourd'hui, c'est lundi.' Method: Model run for 'Days of the week and months'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 20 to 30 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: one page in your learning book.
modules.standard: Say the days and months: at least 4 of 5 attempts correct, said or written, with one real example from home or school.
steps: Step 1, Say the seven days in order: lundi, mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. Notice that French days begin with a small letter. Chant them like a song, clapping on each syllable.

Step 2, Say the twelve months: janvier, février, mars, avril, mai, juin, juillet, août, septembre, octobre, novembre, décembre. Months also use small letters. Say them in groups of four, then all twelve without stopping.

Step 3, Ask and answer. Quel jour est-ce aujourd'hui ? [What day is it today?] Aujourd'hui, c'est mardi. [Today it is Tuesday.] Demain, c'est mercredi. [Tomorrow it is Wednesday.] Hier, c'était lundi. [Yesterday it was Monday.] Use a classroom calendar.

Step 4, Talk about birthdays. Quand est ton anniversaire ? [When is your birthday?] Mon anniversaire est en mars. [My birthday is in March.] Mon anniversaire est le dix mai. [My birthday is on the tenth of May.] Ask three classmates and note their months.

Step 5, Fix an error. A child writes Lundi, Mardi with capital letters, as in English. Correction: lundi, mardi. Another slip is dimanche sounding like dee-manch with a hard English sound; keep the soft French sound of ch.

Step 6, Your turn: say today's day, tomorrow's day and your birthday month. Model answer: Aujourd'hui, c'est jeudi. Demain, c'est vendredi. Mon anniversaire est en octobre. [Today is Thursday. Tomorrow is Friday. My birthday is in October.]

ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
